interface.name: nextspace_shell_v1

description.summary: session-authorized desktop window control

interface.description:
Only the Wayland connection supplied by the session supervisor can see or bind this global. An application ID, PID or same-user public connection grants no authority. Application names and titles are untrusted metadata.
On binding and on snapshot, reset starts a complete enumeration, window describes each mapped toplevel, and done ends the batch. Later window and closed events update this state by ID. IDs are compositor-local and must not be persisted between compositor sessions. Requests for stale IDs are ignored. Coordinates use logical desktop units with a top-left origin.
The supervisor retains a private broker descriptor, separate from the shell. It can replace the authorized connection after a shell crash. The new shell receives a fresh snapshot; compositor and other clients survive. The old connection is closed on replacement. Loss of the broker revokes the shell connection. A compositor restart requires a new session.

event.name: window_info

description.summary: additional presentation metadata for a window

event.description: Sent immediately after each window event. client_id and style are client-supplied; match client_id only within an authenticated native PID. A zero title_height means no supported client frame for shading.

request.name: set_presented

description.summary: control shell presentation without changing application state

request.description: Suppress or restore a mapped window in scene rendering, hit testing and focus selection. This preserves its buffers, geometry, minimization and AppKit state. The shell uses it for Dock/IconYard presentation. It is not an application hide notification. State survives shell replacement; activate restores presentation as well as minimization and shading.

request.name: set_level

description.summary: assign compositor stacking for desktop icons

request.description: Uses the same logical stacking levels as the application protocol, with values clamped to -1000 through 1000. Desktop policy can place a running application's icon in the Dock without changing its AppKit window state. This grants neither shell nor session-lock authority to that application.

request.name: order

description.summary: raise or lower within the existing stacking level

request.description: An above value of zero lowers the window; any other value raises it. This never changes its level, focus, geometry or application state.

event.name: pointer_focus

description.summary: compositor window currently under the pointer

event.description: Reports zero for the desktop, or the mapped toplevel owning the focused surface, including its popups. Sent after the initial snapshot and when the target changes. Desktop policy uses this to raise and lower the Dock with its configured delays, including icons owned by other applications. Pointer focus is independent of keyboard activation.

request.name: configure_outputs

description.summary: create a complete, revision-checked output transaction

request.description: Every connected head must appear exactly once. At least one must remain enabled, and exactly one enabled head must be primary. Stale revisions fail without changing hardware. Only one applied transaction may await confirmation. Destroying it or losing the shell restores the previous layout. Hotplug cancels it and restores surviving heads before recovery.

event.name: output

description.summary: physical mode and independent logical output state

event.description: IDs last for this compositor connection only. Names identify connectors; make/model/serial describe hardware. Persist these together, never the ID. Pixel modes are untransformed. Logical bounds use top-left desktop units, scale is an integer numerator over 120, and transform is wl_output.transform. All head, identity and mode events form one batch ending in outputs_done.

request.name: set_keyboard

description.summary: apply validated xkbcommon rules and repeat settings

request.description: Rule strings are bounded and compiled before changing any device. Repeat delay is milliseconds and rate is hertz; zero rate disables repeat. Numlock is an explicit Boolean. Settings apply to present and new keyboards.

request.name: set_pointer

description.summary: libinput acceleration, independent of X11 thresholds

request.description: Speed is libinput's normalized -1 through 1 value. Profile is adaptive=0 or flat=1. Unsupported physical-device combinations fail and restore the preceding settings. The saved intent also applies to newly added devices. Toolkit drag thresholds and double-click timing remain logical settings.

request.name: set_background

description.summary: set the opaque desktop color

request.description: RGB components are normalized 0..1 values. Invalid components leave the preceding color unchanged. Every request replies with the current color. The compositor draws it below windows across the complete output layout.

request.name: configure_desktops

description.summary: set the desktop count

request.description: Counts from 1 through 32 are accepted. Removing desktops moves their windows to the final remaining desktop. Invalid requests leave state unchanged. Each desktop request replies with desktops.

event.name: interactive_move

description.summary: icon placement tracking

event.description: Standard serial-validated interactive moves of application and miniwindow icons report begin, end or cancellation. Coordinates are logical desktop top-left. The shell suspends automatic placement while tracking; only end persists the new position. Cancellation restores the original position. A snapshot includes begin for a move in progress. cancel_move affects only the current icon grab with the matching id. Primary output bounds travel with the event so a later output change cannot reinterpret the drop.

request.name: set_shortcuts

description.summary: atomically replace desktop key bindings

request.description: The array contains exactly 18 native-endian uint32 pairs, indexed by shortcut_action: XKB keysym followed by a modifier mask. The mask uses Shift=1, Control=4, Alt=8 and Logo=64. A zero keysym and mask disable an action. Nonzero bindings must be unique. Symbols use the active keyboard layout's unshifted level; lock modifiers do not affect matching. Invalid arrays preserve every preceding binding. input_result replies with the matching serial. Disconnecting the shell retains the bindings.

request.name: set_output_insets

description.summary: reserve logical output edges for desktop components

request.description: Only the authorized shell can set these nonnegative logical insets. Each value must be at most 4096; unknown heads and invalid values are ignored. Intent survives shell replacement and output configuration rollback, and is discarded when the head disappears. If opposing insets would consume more than half an output axis, that axis uses its full extent until a larger layout permits the reservation again. Maximized windows use the resulting work area; fullscreen windows use the complete output. Floating windows retain their chosen frames.

event.name: output_work_area

description.summary: effective work area in logical desktop coordinates

event.description: Sent in each output inventory batch after its output event. Disabled heads have an empty work area. Insets are logical and do not rotate with the physical panel. They do not change the output configuration revision.

request.name: set_maximized_drag_mode

description.summary: preserve the existing DragMaximizedWindow preference

request.description: Move (the default) retains maximized size and state, including the saved floating frame. RestoreGeometry restores the floating size with the pointer at the same horizontal fraction of its title bar. Unmaximize clears the state while retaining the current size. NoMove rejects the move. Fullscreen windows never move or resize interactively. Escape cancels a move and restores its preceding geometry and state. Invalid modes are ignored. Changing the mode cancels an active move; the chosen mode survives replacement of the authorized shell.

request.name: set_double_click_time

description.summary: share the existing toolkit double-click interval

request.description: Publish GSDoubleClickTime in milliseconds for compositor-owned frame gestures. This adds no stored preference. Values in 1..60000 are valid; other values are ignored. The default is 350 ms, matching the legacy window manager's fallback until Workspace publishes the user's setting. Changing the interval clears an incomplete click pair. The interval survives replacement of the authorized shell.

request.name: set_title_appearance

description.summary: preserve existing window-title appearance preferences

request.description: The font is the existing WindowTitleFont Fontconfig pattern. Explicit antialias properties override the UseAntialiasedText fallback flag. Pixel sizes remain logical; point sizes use 96 logical DPI unless the pattern supplies an explicit DPI. Empty or invalid patterns, effective pixel sizes outside (0,512], antialiased values above 1 and unknown justification values are ignored. Valid changes repaint existing server titles without a client commit and survive shell replacement. The default remains Helvetica bold 12 logical pixels, monochrome and centered. Client decorations retain their application font settings.

request.name: lock

description.summary: request a session-owned authenticated lock

request.description: Immediately hide ordinary surfaces and input, then ask the private session supervisor to start its configured locker. This request never unlocks. Locker failure keeps the desktop hidden; only the authorized ext-session-lock connection can unlock after authentication.

request.name: set_output_gamma

description.summary: set a hardware output power curve through the authorized shell

request.description: Gamma channels are exponents in 0.1..10 and brightness is in 0..2. The ramp uses min(pow(position, channel) * brightness, 1), preserving SystemKit's existing convention. Unknown, disabled or unsupported heads, invalid values, and requests during a pending layout are ignored. Failed backend test/commit leaves the published settings unchanged. Every request replies with an output snapshot followed by its serial's result. Settings survive shell replacement and mode changes; they are discarded when the output disappears. No software fallback is reported as hardware gamma support.

event.name: output_gamma

description.summary: gamma capability and accepted values in an output inventory batch

event.description: ramp_size is zero when hardware gamma is unavailable. Values describe the compositor's accepted curve, with one as the initial channel and brightness values. This event precedes outputs_done.

interface.name: nextspace_output_configuration_v1

description.summary: compositor-owned test, apply, confirm and rollback

interface.description: Set each head once before test or apply. Test leaves the object editable only by destruction and recreation; apply may follow a successful test. Apply starts the compositor deadline (1000 to 30000 milliseconds). Confirm keeps the state; cancel or destroy reverts it. A settings process need not stay alive for rollback. Results use status values below; reasons are for diagnostics, and clients provide their own user-facing messages.
